stories.headline: US Sends Iran 15-Point Ceasefire Plan via Pakistan as Trump Declares 'We've Won This'

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration sent Iran a 15-point ceasefire proposal covering sanctions relief, civilian nuclear cooperation, rollback of Iran's nuclear program, IAEA monitoring, missile limits, and Hormuz shipping access.
key_facts.excerpt: The Pakistani officials described the proposal broadly as touching on sanctions relief, civilian nuclear cooperation, a rollback of Iran's nuclear program, monitoring by the International Atomic Energy Agency, missile limits and access for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: The plan was delivered to Iran by Pakistan, which has offered to host renewed negotiations between Washington and Tehran.
key_facts.excerpt: A 15-point peace plan has been offered to Iran by intermediaries from Pakistan, as US President Donald Trump plans to deploy more troops to the Middle East.

key_facts.fact: Trump told reporters 'We've won this. This war has been won' and claimed Iran had offered a 'prize' related to oil and gas, while Iran's parliament speaker denied any negotiations with the US.
key_facts.excerpt: President Trump said on Tuesday Iran made a valuable offer to reach a deal with the United States, in talks that Iran has denied are taking place. 'We've won this. This war has been won,' Trump said.

key_facts.fact: An Iranian military spokesperson mocked US ceasefire attempts on Wednesday, insisting that the Americans were 'only negotiating with themselves.'
key_facts.excerpt: An Iranian military spokesperson mocked U.S. attempts at a ceasefire deal Wednesday, insisting that the Americans were only negotiating with themselves.

key_facts.fact: The US-Israeli war on Iran, dubbed Operation Epic Fury, is now in its fourth week after launching on February 28, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: US-Israeli war on Iran now in its fourth week.

stories.headline: Israel Announces Seizure of Southern Lebanon Up to Litani River as 'Defensive Buffer'

key_facts.fact: Defense Minister Israel Katz announced Israeli forces would 'control the remaining bridges and the security zone up to the Litani,' a river 30km north of the border, amounting to nearly a tenth of Lebanon's territory.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel will occupy southern Lebanon up to the Litani River to create a 'defensive buffer,' Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Tuesday, spelling out for the first time Israel's intent to seize territory amounting to nearly a tenth of Lebanon.

key_facts.fact: Israel has destroyed five bridges over the Litani River since March 13 and accelerated demolition of homes in Lebanese border villages.
key_facts.excerpt: Since March 13, Israel has demolished five bridges crossing the Litani River. The military has also accelerated demolition of homes in Lebanese border villages.

key_facts.fact: Hezbollah called the Israeli occupation an 'existential threat' to the Lebanese state. Senior lawmaker Hassan Fadlallah said: 'We have no choice but to confront this aggression and cling to the land.'
key_facts.excerpt: Senior Hezbollah lawmaker Hassan Fadlallah said any Israeli occupation south of the Litani would be met with resistance. 'We have no choice but to confront this aggression and cling to the land,' he told Reuters.

key_facts.fact: Israeli strikes have killed over 1,072 people in Lebanon including 121 children, and displaced more than one million people since the escalation began.
key_facts.excerpt: Since then, 1,072 people have been killed in Lebanon, according to the Lebanese health ministry, including at least 121 children and 42 health workers. More than a million people have been displaced.

key_facts.fact: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for formal annexation of southern Lebanon, declaring 'the new Israeli border must be the Litani.'
key_facts.excerpt: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for formal annexation of southern Lebanon, declaring 'the new Israeli border must be the Litani.'

stories.headline: Russia Launches Record 948 Drones at Ukraine in 24 Hours, Signaling Spring Offensive

key_facts.fact: Russia launched nearly 1,000 strike drones (948) at Ukraine over a 24-hour period on March 24, the largest aerial attack since the war began, breaking the previous record of 728 drones.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's air force said it had detected nearly 1,000 Shahed and other strike drones in one day. Kyiv's latest account breaks Russia's previous launch record of 728 such drones.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine intercepted or disabled 906 of the drones at a 95.5% success rate.
key_facts.excerpt: It said it shot down or disabled 906 of them, at an interception rate of 95.5%.

key_facts.fact: At least six people were killed and 46 injured across Ukraine, with strikes hitting civilian areas including near the 17th century St. Andrew's Church in Lviv.
key_facts.excerpt: A major Russian drone and missile attack on civilian areas of Ukraine killed six people and injured at least 46, officials said Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy said the scale of the strikes showed Putin 'has no real intention of ending this war' and called for stronger international pressure on Moscow.
key_facts.excerpt: Volodymyr Zelensky said the scale of the strikes showed Russia's Vladimir Putin 'has no real intention of ending this war' and called for the international community to exert stronger pressure on Moscow.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's military reported total Russian losses on March 24 included 1,220 personnel, 2,459 UAVs destroyed, and 51 artillery systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Total russian military losses on March 24, 2026: 1,220 personnel, 2,459 UAVs, and 51 artillery systems.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine retaliated with its own record attack, with Russia's Defense Ministry reporting it shot down 389 incoming Ukrainian drones in the largest overnight attack on Russian territory since the war began.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian air defenses downed 389 incoming Ukrainian drones, Russia's Defense Ministry said Wednesday, in what was the largest reported overnight attack on Russian regions and Crimea since Moscow's forces invaded Ukraine.

stories.headline: Pentagon Deploys 2,000 82nd Airborne Troops to Middle East, Total Reinforcements Near 7,000

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon ordered about 2,000 soldiers from the 82nd Airborne Division's Immediate Response Force to deploy to the Middle East, including Maj. Gen. Brandon Tegtmeier and two battalions of ~800 soldiers each.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 1,000 troops from the 82nd Airborne Division... The force would include a battalion of the 1st Brigade Combat Team as well as Maj. Gen. Brandon Tegtmeier, the division's commander, and division staff.

key_facts.fact: The 82nd Airborne is trained to parachute into hostile or contested territory to secure key positions and airfields, distinguishing this from prior Marine deployments focused on embassy support and evacuation.
key_facts.excerpt: The soldiers of the 82nd Airborne, based at Fort Bragg in North Carolina, are trained to parachute into hostile or contested territory to secure key territory and airfields.

key_facts.fact: Combined with 4,500+ Marines already en route, total additional ground forces dispatched since the conflict started approaches 7,000, supplementing the 50,000 troops already assigned to Operation Epic Fury.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump on Tuesday approved the deployment of at least 1,000 soldiers from the Army's 82nd Airborne Division to the Middle East, adding ground forces to a broader U.S. buildup in the region.

key_facts.fact: The Senate Armed Services Committee is scheduled to receive a classified briefing from Pentagon officials on Wednesday regarding the deployment.
key_facts.excerpt: Members of the Senate Armed Services Committee are scheduled to receive a classified briefing from Pentagon officials Wednesday on Capitol Hill.

stories.headline: Iran Imposes $2M Transit Toll on Hormuz Shipping and Turns Back Container Vessel

key_facts.fact: Iran has begun charging transit fees of up to $2 million per voyage on commercial vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz, creating an informal toll on the waterway that normally carries a fifth of the world's oil and gas.
key_facts.excerpt: Payments of as much as $2 million per voyage are being sought on an adhoc basis, effectively creating an informal toll on the waterway.

key_facts.fact: The IRGC Navy turned back containership SELEN departing from Sharjah to Karachi near the Hormuz approach, with IRGC Rear Admiral Tangsiri claiming all vessels must now coordinate passage with Iran's maritime authorities.
key_facts.excerpt: Rear Admiral Alireza Tangsiri, commander of the IRGC Navy, said the vessel was turned back for failing to comply with 'legal protocols' and lacking permission to transit the strait. He added that all vessels must now coordinate passage with Iran's maritime authorities.

key_facts.fact: Only a trickle of vessels have crossed the waterway since the war began, many of them Iranian-linked. Iran's parliament is advancing a proposal to formalize the toll as a 'secure shipping route' fee.
key_facts.excerpt: Only a trickle of vessels have crossed the waterway since the war, many of them Iranian-linked vessels.

key_facts.fact: A vessel using a false identity stolen from a scrapped ship has begun operating a shuttle service believed to transport Iranian oil through Hormuz, exploiting AIS tracking and a clean IMO number to bypass compliance checks.
key_facts.excerpt: A vessel using a false identity from a scrapped ship is shuttling likely Iranian oil through the Strait of Hormuz via ship-to-ship transfers off Oman.

stories.headline: Denmark's Social Democrats Win Election but Slump to Worst Result Since 1903, No Majority

key_facts.fact: Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's Social Democrats won the most votes with 21.9% but suffered their worst result since 1903, down from 27.6% in the 2022 election.
key_facts.excerpt: Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's Social Democrats won the most votes in Tuesday's Danish general election but slumped to its weakest performance since 1903.

key_facts.fact: The Liberals (Venstre) also had their worst showing in over a century with 10.1%, falling behind the Green Left SF which came second with 11.5% of the vote.
key_facts.excerpt: The Social Democrats' main right-wing rival, the Liberals, also had their worst showing for a century, with just 10.1%, falling behind the Green Left SF.

key_facts.fact: Neither the left-wing nor right-wing bloc secured the 90 seats needed for a majority, setting up coalition talks where centrist former PM Lars Løkke Rasmussen could be kingmaker.
key_facts.excerpt: Left-leaning and right-leaning blocs were likely to fall short of a majority in parliament. If that is the case, experienced Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen — a former prime minister — could play the role of kingmaker.

key_facts.fact: The Danish People's Party (DF) and the Green Left SF were the biggest gainers, with DF rebounding to 9.2% of the vote.
key_facts.excerpt: The Socialist People's Party came second with 11.5 percent, followed by Venstre, the Liberal Party of Denmark, at 10.3 percent, Liberal Alliance at 9.4 percent, and the Danish People's Party at 9.2 percent.

key_facts.fact: The campaign focused on domestic issues rather than Frederiksen's handling of the Greenland crisis triggered by Trump's territorial ambitions.
key_facts.excerpt: A campaign that focused on bread-and-butter issues rather than her handling of the crisis over U.S. President Donald Trump's ambitions toward Greenland.

stories.headline: Epic Games Lays Off 1,000+ Employees Citing Fortnite Engagement Downturn

key_facts.fact: Epic Games is laying off over 1,000 employees, approximately 20% of its workforce, with CEO Tim Sweeney citing 'the downturn in Fortnite engagement that started in 2025' leaving the company 'spending significantly more than we're making.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'The downturn in Fortnite engagement that started in 2025 means we're spending significantly more than we're making, and we have to make major cuts to keep the company funded,' Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney wrote.

key_facts.fact: The layoffs combined with $500 million in identified cost savings from contracting, marketing, and closing open roles are intended to stabilize the company financially.
key_facts.excerpt: 'This layoff, together with over $500 million of identified cost savings in contracting, marketing, and closing some open roles puts us in a more stable place.'

key_facts.fact: Sweeney explicitly stated the layoffs 'aren't related to AI,' citing industry-wide challenges including slower growth, weaker consumer spending, and current consoles selling fewer units than the previous generation.
key_facts.excerpt: Fortnite-maker Epic Games says it is laying off more than 1,000 employees, citing a fall in engagement with its popular online game.

key_facts.fact: Epic recently raised V-Bucks prices, its Fortnite in-game currency, to 'help pay the bills' amid increased operating costs. This follows 830 layoffs in 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: Last week, Epic also increased the price of V-Bucks, the Fortnite in-game currency, saying that 'the cost of running Fortnite has gone up a lot.'

stories.headline: Jamie Dimon Warns AI Could Displace Jobs Faster Than Internet, Calls for Govt-Business Response

key_facts.fact: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned that AI could cost US jobs and suggested the government create an incentive system for businesses to retrain workers, fund early retirement, and relocate displaced employees.
key_facts.excerpt: '[If] all of a sudden it creates unemployment, that's a big problem for society,' Dimon said. 'The government could create a system of incentives that business does the right thing to retrain people, early retirement, moving people.'

key_facts.fact: Dimon warned that AI-driven economic changes may happen faster than other recent technological disruptions like the internet, speaking at the Hill and Valley Forum in Washington alongside Palantir defense chief Mike Gallagher.
key_facts.excerpt: Dimon warned the economic changes driven by AI will happen quickly, warning that they may happen faster than other recent technological advances that disrupted the economy and displaced workers, such as the internet.

key_facts.fact: Dimon said the response 'can't be just government' and must involve private sector collaboration, calling for a system where businesses are incentivized to do 'the right thing' in workforce transition.
key_facts.excerpt: 'I don't know the answer yet, but I would suggest it's the following: It can't be just government. It's got to be business,' Dimon said.

sources.title: Dimon warns on AI job losses, calls for government-business incentives

stories.headline: First Parkinson's Patients Dosed in Phase 2 Trial of NLRP3 Inhibitor Dapansutrile

key_facts.fact: Olatec Therapeutics announced the first two patients have been randomized in DAPA-PD, a 12-month Phase 2 clinical trial of dapansutrile for Parkinson's disease at Cambridge University Hospitals.
key_facts.excerpt: Olatec Therapeutics, Inc., developing one of the most clinically advanced specific oral NLRP3 inhibitors, dapansutrile, today announced that two patients have been randomized in a 12-month clinical trial, named DAPA-PD, for the treatment of Parkinson's disease.

key_facts.fact: The trial is a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study led by Dr. Caroline Williams-Gray, measuring safety, tolerability, and changes in systemic and neuroinflammatory biomarkers including PET brain imaging.
key_facts.excerpt: This milestone launches dapansutrile into Phase 2 clinical development for neurological conditions.

key_facts.fact: Dapansutrile is also in Phase 2/3 for gout, Phase 2 for advanced melanoma (with Duke Cancer Institute and Merck), and Phase 2 for type 2 diabetes, making it one of the broadest NLRP3 inhibitor clinical programs.
key_facts.excerpt: Expanding upon ongoing trials with dapansutrile in rheumatologic diseases (Phase 2/3 gout), oncology (Phase 2 advanced melanoma), and cardiometabolic disorders (Phase 2 type 2 diabetes).

key_facts.fact: The trial is funded by Cure Parkinson's and Van Andel Institute, targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway increasingly linked to neurodegeneration.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO Damaris Skouras stated: 'dapansutrile holds considerable potential as an oral therapy capable of modifying a shared core inflammatory mechanism.'

sources.title: First Parkinson's Patients Treated in Landmark Phase 2 Trial of Dapansutrile
